messages:
June Park: quick design sync — toast timing after save feels too fast in the Console. users missed confirmations during rapid workflows.
Felix Moore: agreed. current duration is 800ms. maybe 1.8s visibility + 200ms fade is better. also placement matters; top-right toasts are easy to miss when modal is centered.
Riya Shah: accessibility: longer toast duration doesn't help SR users; we need aria-live updates for screen readers. visual toast should be accompanied by inline announcement when action happens in modal.
Connor Lee: spacing tokens: toast-anchor-gap uses token spacing-compact-01 (4px). visually that's crowded. propose spacing-compact-03 (12px) between close icon and toast chip when anchored to header.
a11y-bot: a11y reminder: "Aria-live regions must be updated on state change. Do not auto-focus toasts. Ensure dismiss button has aria-label 'Dismiss notification'."
June Park: possible solutions: A) extend toast duration to 1.5s and add inline chip for critical actions; B) keep 800ms but sticky for certain verbs + aria-live; C) anchor inline chip to control so it's spatially connected.
Felix Moore: minor dev note: adding inline chip inside header needs token adjustments — header-padding-token currently 8px, chip requires 12px to avoid overlap. I'll prototype: 
```
.inline-toast { position: absolute; right: calc(var(--close-btn-width) + var(--spacing-compact-02)); top: 8px; }
```
Riya Shah: copy: prefer one-word chips 'Saved', 'Copied' to avoid wrapping. For toaster aria announcements: 'Query copied to clipboard.' keep it short.
Connor Lee: keyboard behavior: keep focus on triggering control. aria-live polite region will announce success. do not move focus to the toast. Also ensure ESC dismisses persistent toasts.
June Park: I'll mock 3 variants in #design: (1) longer transient global toast, (2) inline header chip + short global toast, (3) sticky for destructive actions only. Posting in 40m. Tagging @Felix for implementation and @Riya for a11y signoff. :thumbsup:
